significance: A shrine to Ganesha on the summit of the Rockfort at Tiruchirappalli, reached by steps cut into the rock, whose caves were first excavated by the Pallavas in the 7th century and whose temples were completed by the Nayaks of Madurai under the Vijayanagara Empire. The site is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India and looks out over Trichy, Srirangam and the rivers below.
story: Ganesha is said to have taken the form of a Brahmin boy and set down the image of Ranganatha that Vibhishana was carrying to Lanka, so that it stayed at Srirangam.
